decisions.reason: Published within the September 11–October 10 freshness window, but concerns UK financial-brand loyalty rather than AI tools for conducting research. Customers taking financial questions to AI does not establish a research capability. STRAT7 promotes its own research services and report; the supplied percentages lack sample, fieldwork dates and methods. No cross-post or repeated underlying claim is evident in this batch.

The October 7 article identifies a relevant pilot idea: combining lexical and semantic retrieval to search research-document collections. However, the supplied evidence provides no inspected tool documentation, worked demonstration, retrieval evaluation, cost baseline or setup requirements to substantiate its accuracy, speed and savings claims or feasibility with little technical support. Publication is recent, but no new release or meaningful test is established. The author promotes consulting and a paid course; recommendations are commercially interested practitioner claims. Small-business use, non-English performance and customer-data handling remain unaddressed. No cross-post is evident; its publisher also appears in the MAICON podcast promotion, which supplies no independent corroboration.

The September 30 publication is timely but promotes conference attendance and future podcast recordings on October 14–15, after the as-of date and publication deadline. It supplies no substantive passages evaluating research tools, methods, costs or reliability. The organizer's marketing officer can establish the advertised schedule, not the promised practical impact. In-Ear Insights shares a producer with the Penn candidate; future audio/video cross-posts would require checking and would not constitute independent corroboration.

The October 9 reporting is timely, but recycling robotics does not address gathering or validating customer, competitor or market evidence on a small-business budget. Founder estimates of revenue, comparative efficiency and ROI lack observed deployment results, baselines and evaluation methods; they are commercially interested claims, alongside promotion of participation in the publisher's event. These limitations do not undermine the attributed founder account, but it remains outside scope. No cross-post or repeated underlying claim is evident in this batch.
